draft.title: Technology in farming
card: Farmers use technology to learn what each part of a farm needs. They can then use water and fertiliser where they are needed, not spread them evenly over everything.
Satellite mapping and GIS
Satellite images show how crops are growing across a farm. A geographic information system (GIS) stores this data as layers of maps, such as soil type and crop health, so farmers can compare them.
Sensors
Sensors in the soil or on machines measure things like moisture. They show which areas are dry and which already have enough water.
New crop varieties
Plant breeders develop new varieties that can cope better with conditions such as dry weather or salty soil. These can lift yields where the old varieties struggled.
draft.remember: Technology shows farmers where inputs are needed, and new varieties help crops cope, so yields can rise.

a.q: A farmer uses soil moisture sensors to decide which paddocks to water. How does this technology help?
opts: It shows which areas need water, so none is wasted
It makes rain fall on the driest paddocks
It changes the crop into a new variety
It shows the price the crop will sell for
a.why: Sensors measure moisture, so the farmer can water only the paddocks that need it. They do not change the weather, the crop or the market price.
a.clue: Think about what a sensor measures.

b.q: Priya farms wheat in Western Australia. Satellite images show weak growth in one corner of her farm. A GIS map shows the soil there is low in nutrients. What is the best use of this data?
opts: Add extra fertiliser to that corner only
Add the same fertiliser evenly across the whole farm
Water the whole farm more often
Stop growing wheat on the entire farm
b.why: The satellite images and the GIS map together point to one problem area, so fertiliser can go where it is needed. Spreading it evenly wastes fertiliser on areas that are growing well.
b.clue: The data points to one part of the farm.

a.best: It shows which areas need water, so none is wasted

b.best: Add extra fertiliser to that corner only

problems.detail: The right option claims 'so none is wasted', an absolute the card does not make. The card only says water can go where it is needed rather than evenly. A wording such as 'so less is wasted' would be more accurate.
